# The core library

<!-- covers: LR 15 -->
*Human mode. Agent mode: [Core library, by declaration](../agent/library.md). Generated by

> Preview: the core runtime inventory (LR 15) arrives in v0.4.

This is the reference for the standard library that ships with the compiler: every type and function of the core
package `fortis`, with its signature, what it promises and the effects it has. It is not a tutorial; the chapters
of this guide teach the language, and this page is where you look an operation up. Nothing here is written by
hand: each entry is the library's own declaration and the documentation comment above it, so the page cannot say
something the library does not do. The same facts, as tables for tools, are in
[the agent-mode page](../agent/library.md).

## How to read an entry

The library is one package, `fortis`, made of seven modules. Each section below is a module. `fortis.prelude` is
imported into every module for you; the others you import by name (LR 4.3). Under a module come its types, each
with its operations, and then its free functions.

An entry is the operation's signature followed by what it promises. Read the signature the way you read your own:
`self` is the value the operation is called on, a word before `func` such as `pure` or `try` is a claim the
compiler checks (LR 11.2), and `from self` says the result is a loan of the receiver, so it cannot outlive it
(LR 7.6). Most operations are `trusted`: the toolchain implements them, and the sentence under the signature is
the contract a reviewer signed off (LR 11.3). A cost such as `O(n)` is the bound the contract promises.

*Effects* tell you what calling the operation does beyond computing its result, and what your own function
inherits by calling it (LR 11.1):

- `pure`: written before the effects when the signature claims it: the operation reads nothing from outside its arguments and writes nothing (LR 11.2). The effects after it are what a pure operation may still do, such as allocate or fail.
- `noalloc`: written before the effects when the signature claims it: the operation promises not to allocate (LR 11.4).
- `none`: an operation that does not claim `pure` and has no effect to declare.
- `alloc`: it allocates; it cannot be called from `noalloc` code (LR 11.4).
- `fail`: it is declared `try`: it can fail, and the caller must handle the outcome (LR 10.1).
- `suspend`: it is `async` and can wait (LR 12.3).
- `recovers`: it discards a failure it handled (LR 10.4).
- `block`: it blocks the calling thread (LR 11.1).
- `io`: it reaches the outside world through an authority (LR 11.6).
- `mutate`: it writes storage that tasks share (LR 11.1).
- `nondet`: its result can differ between runs with the same arguments (LR 11.1).
- `writes self`: it changes the value it is called on (`editable self`).

## `fortis.prelude`

You never import this module; every module has it already (LR 4.3). It holds the types you use in every program: the integers and floats, `String` and `StringView`, lists, maps and sets, `Outcome` and `Failure`, the concurrency types, and the built-in interfaces such as `Equatable` and `Displayable`. The everyday text operations (`trim`, `split`, `find`, `replace` and the rest) are members of `String` and `StringView`, so they need no import either. (LR 4.3, LR 6.2, LR 6.10).

### `class Int`

- `pure try func add(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Checked 64-bit two's-complement addition; fails `numeric.overflow` outside [-2^63, 2^63-1]; O(1), no allocation. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func sub(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Checked subtraction; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func mul(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Checked multiplication; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func div(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Truncating division; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0 and `numeric.overflow` for -2^63 / -1; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func rem(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Remainder with the sign of a; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func shiftLeft(a: Int, bits: Int) Int`. A * 2^bits; fails `numeric.shift_range` unless 0 <= bits < 64 and `numeric.overflow` when the result is out of range; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func wrappingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Addition modulo 2^64 into [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func wrappingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Subtraction modulo 2^64; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func wrappingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Multiplication modulo 2^64; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func saturatingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Addition clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func saturatingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Subtraction clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func saturatingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int`. Multiplication clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func validate(value: Int) Int`. The value when it lies in the refinement of the receiver type; fails `refinement.out_of_range` otherwise; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*

### `class Float`

- `pure func sqrt(x: Float) Float`. IEEE 754 binary64 correctly rounded square root; NaN for negative input; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func totalOrder(x: Float) Int64`. The IEEE 754 totalOrder key of x as a signed 64-bit integer; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func bitsEqual(a: Float, b: Float) Bool`. True exactly when a and b have the same 64-bit pattern; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func isNaN(x: Float) Bool`. True exactly for NaN; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Float32`

- `pure func sqrt(x: Float32) Float32`. IEEE 754 binary32 correctly rounded square root; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func isNaN(x: Float32) Bool`. True exactly for NaN; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `enum RoundingMode`

Variants: `HalfEven`, `HalfAwayFromZero`, `TowardZero`, `AwayFromZero`.

### `class Decimal`

- `pure try func add(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal`. The sum at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when it needs more than 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` when the integer part does not fit (6.4); O(digits). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func sub(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal`. The difference at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when needed; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func mul(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal`. The product at the sum of the scales, rounded half to even above 28 fractional digits or 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func div(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal`. The quotient at the largest scale that fits, rounded half to even; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` and `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func rem(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal`. The remainder with the sign of the dividend at the larger operand scale; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` (6.4); O(digits^2). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func round(value: Decimal, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal`. Value rounded to scale by mode; total; O(digits). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func fromFloat(x: Float, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal`. The binary value of x rounded to scale by mode; fails `numeric.overflow` for a non-finite x or an integer part that does not fit (6.4); O(digits). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func scale(self) Int<0..28>`. The number of fractional digits; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class String`

- `pure func from(text: StringView) String`. An owned copy of the view; allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func empty() String` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func scalarCount(self) Int`. The number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func byteCount(self) Int`. The UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func trim(self) StringView from self`. The view without its leading and trailing Unicode White_Space (U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) scalars; a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func trimStart(self) StringView from self`. The view without its leading White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func trimEnd(self) StringView from self`. The view without its trailing White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func find(self, needle: StringView) Int<0..>?`. The scalar offset (the unit of slice and scalarAt) of the first occurrence of needle, null when it does not occur; an empty needle occurs at 0; no allocation; at most O(n * m) in bytes for a text of n bytes and a needle of m. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func contains(self, needle: StringView) Bool`. True exactly when find(needle) is present: an empty needle is contained in every text. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func startsWith(self, prefix: StringView) Bool`. True exactly when the text begins with prefix (an empty prefix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a prefix of m. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func endsWith(self, suffix: StringView) Bool`. True exactly when the text ends with suffix (an empty suffix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a suffix of m. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func split(self, separator: StringView) List[String]`. The pieces between the non-overlapping occurrences of separator, found left to right, as owned strings; a separator at either end gives an empty piece there, a text without the separator gives one piece (itself), and an empty separator occurs nowhere, so it gives one piece; allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func lines(self) List[String]`. The lines of the text as owned strings, each ended by a line feed or by a carriage return and a line feed (neither stays in the line); the text after the last terminator is a line only when it is not empty, so "" has no lines and "a\n" has one; a carriage return not before a line feed stays in the line; allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func replace(self, old: StringView, new: StringView) String`. A copy of the text with every non-overlapping occurrence of old, found left to right, replaced by new; an empty old occurs nowhere, so the copy is unchanged; allocates; O(n) in bytes plus the find cost. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func asciiUpper(self) String`. A copy with the ASCII letters a-z mapped to A-Z and every other scalar unchanged (not Unicode case mapping: that depends on the Unicode version and the language, and changes lengths); allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func asciiLower(self) String`. A copy with the ASCII letters A-Z mapped to a-z and every other scalar unchanged (as asciiUpper); allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func repeat(self, times: Int<0..>) String`. The text written times in a row: "" when times is 0 or the text is empty; allocates; O(times * n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func join(parts: ListView[String], separator: StringView) String`. The parts in order with separator between neighbours: "" for no parts and the part itself for one; allocates; O(total length). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class StringView`

- `pure func scalarCount(self) Int`. The number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func byteCount(self) Int`. The UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

- `pure func trimEnd(self) StringView from self`. The view without its trailing White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure.*

- `pure func endsWith(self, suffix: StringView) Bool`. True exactly when the text ends with suffix (an empty suffix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a suffix of m. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func split(self, separator: StringView) List[String]`. The pieces between the non-overlapping occurrences of separator, found left to right, as owned strings; a separator at either end gives an empty piece there, a text without the separator gives one piece (itself), and an empty separator occurs nowhere, so it gives one piece; allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*

The lines of the text as owned strings, each ended by a line feed or by a carriage return and a line feed (neither stays in the line); the text after the last terminator is a line only when it is not empty, so "" has no lines and "a\n" has one; a carriage return not before a line feed stays in the line; allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func replace(self, old: StringView, new: StringView) String`. A copy of the text with every non-overlapping occurrence of old, found left to right, replaced by new; an empty old occurs nowhere, so the copy is unchanged; allocates; O(n) in bytes plus the find cost. *Effects: pure; alloc.*

- `pure func asciiLower(self) String`. A copy with the ASCII letters A-Z mapped to a-z and every other scalar unchanged (as asciiUpper); allocates; O(n) in bytes. *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class Bytes`

- `pure func byteCount(self) Int`. The length in bytes; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) Byte?`. The byte at index, or null outside [0, byteCount); never allocates; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class BytesView`

- `pure func byteCount(self) Int`. The length in bytes; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The length in bytes (same as byteCount); O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) Byte?`. The byte at index, or null outside [0, byteCount); never allocates; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Scalar`

- `pure func of(text: StringView) Scalar`. The single scalar of a one-scalar view; a constant expression for a literal; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func digitValue(s: Scalar) Int<0..9>?`. The value 0-9 of an ASCII decimal digit, null otherwise; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func hexValue(s: Scalar) Int<0..15>?`. The value 0-15 of an ASCII hexadecimal digit (either case), null otherwise; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Duration`

- `pure func days(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 86400 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) (n bounded by the 64-bit count). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func hours(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 3600 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func minutes(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 60 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func seconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func milliseconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 10^6 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func add(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration`. Sum of the signed 64-bit nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration`. Difference of the nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func multiply(d: Duration, factor: Int) Duration`. The count times factor; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func nanoseconds(self) Int`. The signed 64-bit nanosecond count; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Instant`

### `class Timestamp`

- `pure func epoch() Timestamp`. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as a signed 64-bit nanosecond count of 0; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func add(t: Timestamp, d: Duration) Timestamp`. T + d in nanoseconds since the epoch; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func after(a: Timestamp, b: Timestamp) Bool`. A is strictly later than b; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func before(a: Timestamp, b: Timestamp) Bool`. A is strictly earlier than b; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class List[T]`

- `pure func default() List[T]`. An empty list with no allocation until the first push; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func of(...items: owned T) List[T]`. A list holding the arguments in order; allocates once; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The number of elements; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func push(editable self, item: owned T)`. Appends item; amortised O(1) (capacity doubles), worst case O(n) for the growth step. *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func pop(editable self) T?`. Removes and returns the last element, null when empty; O(1). *Effects: writes self.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the element at index, null outside [0, count); O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func at(self, index: Int) T`. The element at index; fails `collection.index` outside [0, count); O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `try func set(editable self, index: Int, value: owned T)`. Replaces the element at index, dropping the old value; fails `collection.index`; O(1). *Effects: fail, writes self.*
- `func clear(editable self)`. Removes and drops every element; rejected for a linear element type (10.7): consume them instead; O(n). *Effects: writes self.*
- `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func reversed(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func concat(self, other: ListView[T]) List[T] where T implements Copyable` *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func countWhere(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Int` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) List[U] where U: linear` *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) List[T] where T implements Copyable` *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)`. Calls visit with a read loan of every element in order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: none.*
- `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])`. As `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: fail.*
- `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) List[U]`. As `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new list dropped (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the callback per element
U must be non-linear: failure drops earlier results (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3). *Effects: pure; alloc, fail.*
- `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A`. Step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an element, once per element in order, and returns the next accumulator (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A`. As `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for some element; stops at the first one that passes (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for every element; stops at the first one that fails (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?`. The index of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable`. Whether some element equals target (X-479); O(n). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func enumerate(self) List[(Int, T)] where T implements Copyable`. Each element copied with its index, in order (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func zip[U](self, other: ListView[U]) List[(T, U)] where T implements Copyable, U implements Copyable`. Pairs of copies of the elements at the same index of self and other, as many as the shorter has (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, m)). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func take(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the first n elements, all of them when n is at least count(), none when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, count)). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func skip(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the elements after the first n, none when n is at least count(), all when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(count). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func flatMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) List[U]) List[U] where U: linear`. The lists f returns for each element, joined in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the sizes of the lists plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func chunked(self, size: Int<1..>) List[List[T]] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the elements in lists of size elements, the last one shorter when size does not divide count() (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func sortedBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) List[T] where T implements Copyable, K implements Comparable`. Copies of the elements ordered by key(element), smaller keys first, elements with equal keys in their original order (a stable merge sort over indexes); key is called once per element (X-479); allocates; O(n log n) comparisons plus n callbacks. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func groupBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) Map[K, List[T]] where T implements Copyable, K implements Copyable, K implements Hashable, K implements Equatable`. Copies of the elements gathered by key(element) into a Map from each key to its elements in their original order; the keys are in the order they first appear (X-479); allocates; expected O(n) plus n callbacks. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self`. A cursor over read loans of the elements in order; O(1) to create, O(1) per step. *Effects: pure.*
- `func consumeEach(owned self, visit: fn mut(owned T) Void)`. Consumes the list (10.7): no early exit, so no element is left unvisited; an empty list makes no calls
intrinsic: calls visit once per element in order, transferring each element out; O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: none.*

- `pure func next(editable self) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the next element, null at the end; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

- `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) List[U]`. As `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new list dropped (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the callback per element
U must be non-linear: failure drops earlier results (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3). *Effects: pure; alloc, fail.*
- `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A`. Step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an element, once per element in order, and returns the next accumulator (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A`. As `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for some element; stops at the first one that passes (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for every element; stops at the first one that fails (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?`. The index of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable`. Whether some element equals target (X-479); O(n). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func enumerate(self) List[(Int, T)] where T implements Copyable`. Each element copied with its index, in order (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func zip[U](self, other: ListView[U]) List[(T, U)] where T implements Copyable, U implements Copyable`. Pairs of copies of the elements at the same index of self and other, as many as the shorter has (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, m)). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func take(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the first n elements, all of them when n is at least count(), none when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, count)). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func skip(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the elements after the first n, none when n is at least count(), all when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(count). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func flatMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) List[U]) List[U] where U: linear`. The lists f returns for each element, joined in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the sizes of the lists plus the callback per element. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func chunked(self, size: Int<1..>) List[List[T]] where T implements Copyable`. Copies of the elements in lists of size elements, the last one shorter when size does not divide count() (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func sortedBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) List[T] where T implements Copyable, K implements Comparable`. Copies of the elements ordered by key(element), smaller keys first, elements with equal keys in their original order (a stable merge sort over indexes); key is called once per element (X-479); allocates; O(n log n) comparisons plus n callbacks. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func groupBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) Map[K, List[T]] where T implements Copyable, K implements Copyable, K implements Hashable, K implements Equatable`. Copies of the elements gathered by key(element) into a Map from each key to its elements in their original order; the keys are in the order they first appear (X-479); allocates; expected O(n) plus n callbacks. *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class Array[T, N]`

- `pure func filled(value: T) Array[T, N]`. N copies of value; O(N), inline storage. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. N; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func set(editable self, index: Int, value: owned T)`. Replaces the element at index; O(1). *Effects: writes self.*
- `pure func asView(self) ListView[T] from self`. The array's elements as a read-only view, which has `get`, `each`, `map`, `fold` and the rest of ListView's methods (X-578, D-542); O(1), no copy. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the element at index, null outside [0, count) (X-578, D-542); O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Map[K, V]`

- `pure func default() Map[K, V] where K implements Hashable`. An empty map; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func get(self, key: K) (alias V from self)?`. A read loan of the value for key, null when absent (on a Map[String, V] the key is a StringView, which hashes and compares as the String with its text: LR 6.7, X-345); expected O(1) under the release's fixed hash function. *Effects: pure.*
- `func set(editable self, key: owned K, value: owned V)`. Inserts or replaces the value for key, dropping a replaced value; amortised expected O(1). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The number of keys; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func containsKey(self, key: K) Bool`. Whether key has an entry (a StringView key on a Map[String, V], as `get`); expected O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func remove(editable self, key: K) V?`. Removes the entry for key and returns its value, which the caller now owns; null when there is none. The entries after it keep their order and move up one place, so the cost is O(n) in the entries after it (a StringView key on a Map[String, V], as `get`). *Effects: writes self.*
- `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool where K implements Hashable` *Effects: pure.*
- `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(K, V) Void) where K implements Hashable`. Calls visit with a read loan of every key and its value in first-insertion order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per entry. *Effects: none.*
- `pure func keys(self) List[K] where K implements Hashable, K implements Copyable`. Copies of the keys in first-insertion order (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func values(self) List[V] where K implements Hashable, V implements Copyable`. Copies of the values in first-insertion order (X-479); allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class Set[T]`

- `pure func default() Set[T] where T implements Hashable`. An empty set; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func add(editable self, item: owned T) Bool`. Inserts item, true when it was absent; amortised expected O(1). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func contains(self, item: T) Bool`. Membership (a StringView item on a Set[String], as `Map.get`'s key); expected O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The number of items; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func remove(editable self, item: T) Bool`. Removes item, true when it was present. The items after it keep their order and move up one place, so the cost is O(n) in the items after it (a StringView item on a Set[String], as `Map.get`'s key). *Effects: writes self.*
- `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool where T implements Hashable` *Effects: pure.*
- `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void) where T implements Hashable`. Calls visit with a read loan of every item in first-insertion order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: none.*
- `pure func union(self, other: Set[T]) Set[T] where T implements Hashable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the items of self, then of the items of other that self lacks, in that order (X-479); allocates; expected O(n + m). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func intersection(self, other: Set[T]) Set[T] where T implements Hashable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the items of self that other also holds, in self's order (X-479); allocates; expected O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func difference(self, other: Set[T]) Set[T] where T implements Hashable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the items of self that other lacks, in self's order (X-479); allocates; expected O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

`Optional` is not a type a program names: it holds the helpers of a `T?` receiver, so `maybe.map(f)` is `Optional.map(maybe, f)`.

- `pure func map[T, U](value: T?, f: pure fn(T) U) U? where U: linear`. The present value is lent to f and f's result is the present result; null stays null and f is not called (X-479); O(1) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*

- `pure func create() Must`. A zero-sized linear witness; O(1), no allocation. *Effects: pure.*

### `class Outcome[T]`

- `pure func success(value: owned T) Outcome[T]`. An outcome holding value; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func failure(f: owned Failure) Outcome[T]`. An outcome holding f; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func collect(list: owned List[Outcome[T]]) List[T]`. The successes in order when every element succeeds, otherwise the first failure in order, consuming every other element's obligation; T must be non-linear (10.7, E-OBL-003); O(n) (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3). *Effects: pure; alloc, fail.*
- `pure func map[U](owned self, f: pure fn(T) U) Outcome[U] where U: linear`. Consumes the outcome; a success becomes the success of f applied to a read loan of its value, a failure passes through unchanged and f is not called (X-479); O(1) plus the callback
T must be non-linear: the callback borrows a payload that is then dropped (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Shared[T]`

- `pure func create(value: owned T) Shared[T]`. A reference-counted owner holding value, strong count 1; allocates once; O(1). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func retain(self) Shared[T]`. A new strong handle, strong count + 1; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func downgrade(self) Weak[T]`. A weak handle to the same value; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Weak[T]`

- `func upgrade(self) Shared[T]?`. A strong handle when the value is alive, null after the last strong handle was dropped; O(1). *Effects: nondet.*
- `pure func retain(self) Weak[T]`. A new weak handle; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Mutex[T]`

- `pure func create(value: owned T) Mutex[T]`. A mutex owning value; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `async try func lock(self) MutexGuard[T] from self`. An exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, suspending until the lock is free; fails `concurrency.poisoned` if a holder was terminated by a defect (unreachable on the interpreter, where a defect ends the program). *Effects: fail, suspend.*
- `try func lockBlocking(self) MutexGuard[T] from self`. An exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, blocking the thread until free (the `block` effect); fails `concurrency.poisoned`. *Effects: fail, block.*

### `class MutexGuard[T]`

- `pure func get(self) T where T implements Copyable`. A copy of the protected value, read through the exclusive guard (12.7); allocates when the value owns heap storage. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `func set(self, value: owned T)`. Replaces the protected value with value and drops the old one; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1). *Effects: mutate.*
- `func replace(self, value: owned T) T`. Replaces the protected value with value and returns the old one, which the caller now owns; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1). *Effects: mutate.*

- `func store(self, value: Int)`. Replaces the value (seqcst); O(1). *Effects: mutate.*
- `func fetchAdd(self, delta: Int) Int`. Adds delta with wrapping and returns the previous value (seqcst); O(1). *Effects: mutate.*

- `func store(self, value: Bool)`. Replaces the value (seqcst); O(1). *Effects: mutate.*

- `func launchParallel[T](self, work: owned Future[T]) Task[T] where T: linear`. A task running work on the parallel pool (12.5); the environment is Shareable; O(1). *Effects: alloc.*

- `func detach[T](self, task: owned Task[T], supervisor: Supervisor)`. Removes task from the scope and hands its join obligation to supervisor (12.5); O(1). *Effects: io.*

## `fortis.text`

Building and inspecting text. Import what you use, for example `import fortis.text { Builder }`. It holds `Builder`, which accumulates text a piece at a time, the one-character `Scalar`, `graphemes`, which counts what a reader sees as characters, and `Text.words`. (LR 6.6).

### `class Builder`

- `pure func create() Builder`. An empty builder; O(1). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `func append(editable self, text: StringView)`. Appends the view; amortised O(len). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func appendLine(editable self, text: StringView)`. Appends the view and a line feed; amortised O(len). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func appendScalar(editable self, s: Scalar)`. Appends one scalar; amortised O(1). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func finish(self) String`. The accumulated text as an owned String; O(total length). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class Scalar`

- `pure func of(text: StringView) Scalar`. The single scalar of a one-scalar view; a constant expression for a literal; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func digitValue(s: Scalar) Int<0..9>?`. The value 0-9 of an ASCII decimal digit, null otherwise; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func hexValue(s: Scalar) Int<0..15>?`. The value 0-15 of an ASCII hexadecimal digit (either case), null otherwise; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Text`

- `pure func words(text: StringView) List[String]`. The maximal runs of non-whitespace scalars (Unicode White_Space), in order, as owned strings; allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### Functions and aspects

- `pure func graphemes(text: StringView) Int`. The number of extended grapheme clusters (UAX #29, the rules GB3-GB9c and GB11-GB13 over combining marks, ZWJ sequences and regional-indicator pairs; Hangul syllable rules GB6-GB8 are not yet implemented); O(n). *Effects: pure.*

## `fortis.collections`

Algorithms over collections that the prelude's core list, map and set operations do not cover. Import what you use, for example `import fortis.collections { sorted }`. (LR 6.7).

### `class Deque[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`front` holds the items from the front end, the first item last, so popping the front is its `pop`; `back` holds the
rest, the last item last. An end that runs dry takes half of the other end's items over, which costs as many moves as
the pushes that filled that end, so both ends are amortised O(1) and no item is copied.

- `pure func default() Deque[T]`. An empty deque; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) Deque[T]`. A deque of the items of the list in order, the first at the front, taking the list's storage; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The number of items; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool`. Whether the deque holds no item; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func pushBack(editable self, item: owned T)`. Adds item after the last one; amortised O(1). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func pushFront(editable self, item: owned T)`. Adds item before the first one; amortised O(1). *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func popFront(editable self) T?`. Removes and returns the first item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance. *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `func popBack(editable self) T?`. Removes and returns the last item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance. *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the item at index, counted from the front, null outside [0, count); O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func peekFront(self) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the first item, null when empty; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func peekBack(self) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the last item, null when empty; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self`. A cursor over read loans of the items from the front to the back, the items of `front` last to first and then those of `back`; the cursor lists them when it is made, O(count), and each step is O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)`. Calls visit with a read loan of every item from the front to the back; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: none.*
- `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])`. As `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: fail.*
- `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) Deque[U]`. A deque of the results of f for every item, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) Deque[U]`. As `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new deque dropped; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: pure; alloc, fail.*
- `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Deque[T] where T implements Copyable`. A deque of copies of the items keep is true for, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A`. Step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an item, once per item from the front to the back, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A`. As `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item. *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for some item; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for every item; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?`. The position, counted from the front, of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable`. Whether some item equals target; O(n). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. A list of copies of the items from the front to the back; allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### `class SortedSet[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`items` holds the members in ascending order, each once, so a lookup is a binary search over `get`, O(log n). Making
room for a member or closing the gap a removal leaves moves the members after it, one pop and one push each, so `add`
and `remove` are O(n) in the members after the one added or removed; the set operations merge two ascending lists in
one pass, O(n + m).

- `pure func default() SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable`. An empty set; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable`. A set of the items of the list, each once; the list's duplicates are dropped; O(n) times the members each add moves. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func count(self) Int`. The number of members; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool`. Whether the set has no member; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `func add(editable self, item: owned T) Bool where T implements Comparable`. Adds item, true when it was absent; O(log n) to find its place and O(n) in the members after it to make room. *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func contains(self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable`. Whether item is a member; O(log n). *Effects: pure.*
- `func remove(editable self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable`. Removes item, true when it was a member; O(log n) to find it and O(n) in the members after it to close the gap. *Effects: alloc, writes self.*
- `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the smallest member, null when empty; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func last(self) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the largest member, null when empty; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the member at index in ascending order, null outside [0, count); O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self`. The cursor of the sorted list, so a `for` visits the members from the smallest to the largest; O(1) to make, O(1) per step. *Effects: pure.*
- `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)`. Calls visit with a read loan of every member in ascending order; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per member. *Effects: none.*
- `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A`. Step gets a read loan of the accumulator and a member, once per member in ascending order, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per member. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for some member; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool`. Whether holds is true for every member; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?`. A read loan of the smallest member holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback. *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable`. A list of copies of the members in ascending order; allocates; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func between(self, low: T, high: T) List[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable`. A list of copies of the members from low up to, but not including, high, in ascending order; empty when high is not above low; allocates; O(log n) to find low and O(k) for the k members copied. *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func union(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the members of self and of other, each once, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func intersection(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the members both self and other hold, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m). *Effects: pure; alloc.*
- `pure func difference(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable`. Copies of the members of self that other lacks, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m). *Effects: pure; alloc.*

### Functions and aspects

- `pure func sorted(items: ListView[Int]) List[Int]`. Bottom-up merge sort: stable, O(n log n) comparisons and copies, O(n) extra space. *Effects: pure.*

Small integer helpers. Import what you use, for example `import fortis.numeric { min, max }`. (LR 6.4).

- `pure func abs(value: Int) Int<0..>` *Effects: pure.*

## `fortis.time`

Durations and timestamps, with checked arithmetic. Import what you use. (LR 15).

### `class Duration`

- `pure func days(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 86400 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) (n bounded by the 64-bit count). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func hours(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 3600 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func minutes(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 60 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func seconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func milliseconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration`. N * 10^6 nanoseconds; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func add(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration`. Sum of the signed 64-bit nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration`. Difference of the nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func multiply(d: Duration, factor: Int) Duration`. The count times factor; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func nanoseconds(self) Int`. The signed 64-bit nanosecond count; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

### `class Instant`

### `class Timestamp`

- `pure func epoch() Timestamp`. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z as a signed 64-bit nanosecond count of 0; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func add(t: Timestamp, d: Duration) Timestamp`. T + d in nanoseconds since the epoch; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func after(a: Timestamp, b: Timestamp) Bool`. A is strictly later than b; O(1). *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func before(a: Timestamp, b: Timestamp) Bool`. A is strictly earlier than b; O(1). *Effects: pure.*

## `fortis.money`

An amount of a currency, with exact decimal arithmetic. Import what you use. (LR 15).

### `enum Currency derive Equatable`

Variants: `GBP`, `EUR`, `USD`.

### `error CurrencyMismatch`

### `class Money`

- `pure func of(currency: Currency, amount: Decimal) Money` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure func zero(currency: Currency) Money` *Effects: pure.*
- `pure try func add(a: Money, b: Money) Money` *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func subtract(a: Money, b: Money) Money` *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func multiply(money: Money, factor: Int) Money`. The amount times factor at the amount's scale (an Int has scale 0), rounded half to even when it needs more than 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure try func divide(money: Money, divisor: Int<1..>) Money`. The amount divided by divisor at the largest scale that fits, rounded half to even; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2). *Effects: pure; fail.*
- `pure func greaterThan(a: Money, b: Money) Bool`. Ordered within one currency; amounts in different currencies are incomparable, so greaterThan is false. *Effects: pure.*

## `fortis.host`

The capabilities a program receives from its host (the file system, the network, the clock, the console and the rest), the `Path` they take, and `Secret`. Each capability is an authority: a function that holds none cannot reach the outside world (LR 11.6). (LR 11.6, LR 15).

### `class Path`

- `pure try func parse(text: String) Path`. A path from its text; fails `path.invalid` for empty text or text containing NUL; O(n). *Effects: pure; alloc, fail.*

### `class Secret[T]`

### `class SecretAccess implements Authority`

### `class FileSystem implements Authority`

- `try func readText(self, path: Path) String`. The UTF-8 contents of path below this root; fails `fs.outside_root` when the path is absolute or escapes the root, `fs.not_found`, `fs.not_a_file` or `fs.invalid_text`. Development adapter: the root is a fresh empty temporary directory per run, or FORTIS_DEV_ROOT when set; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*
- `try func writeAll(self, path: Path, text: StringView)`. Replaces the contents of path with text, creating the file; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found` (missing parent directory); blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*
- `try func readAll(self, path: Path) Bytes`. The bytes of path; fails `fs.outside_root`, `fs.not_found` or `fs.not_a_file`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*
- `try func open(self, path: Path) File`. An open file for reading; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*
- `try func create(self, path: Path) File`. An open file for writing, created or truncated; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*
- `func subtree(self, path: Path) FileSystem`. A FileSystem confined below path; a path that escapes this root yields a confinement that refuses every operation with `fs.outside_root` (attenuation never widens). *Effects: alloc, io.*

### `class File`

- `try func readAll(editable self) Bytes`. The remaining bytes of a file opened for reading; fails `fs.closed` after close and `fs.wrong_mode` on a file opened for writing; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, writes self.*
- `try func writeAll(editable self, data: BytesView)`. Appends data to a file opened for writing; fails `fs.closed` after close and `fs.wrong_mode` on a file opened for reading; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: fail, block, writes self.*
- `func close(editable self)`. Closes the file; closing twice has no effect; dropping an open file closes it. *Effects: writes self.*

### `class Network implements Authority`

- `try func resolve(self, host: StringView) String`. The address of host. Development adapter: offline; `localhost` resolves to 127.0.0.1 and every other host fails `network.unreachable`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*

### `class Clock implements Authority`

- `async func sleep(self, duration: Duration)`. Suspends the task for duration of the clock's time (a cancellation point, 12.4). Development adapter: virtual time on the controlled scheduler. *Effects: suspend, io.*
- `func now(self) Timestamp`. The current instant in UTC (nondet). Development adapter: the system clock; a frozen clock returns its instant. *Effects: io, nondet.*
- `func frozen(self, instant: Timestamp) Clock`. A clock whose now() is always instant (for tests and replay). *Effects: io.*
- `try func elapsedSince(self, earlier: Timestamp) Duration`. Now() minus earlier; fails `clock.future` when earlier is after now(). *Effects: fail, io, nondet.*

### `class Random implements Authority`

- `func below(self, bound: Int<1..>) Int<0..>`. A uniformly distributed integer in [0, bound) (nondet; rejection sampling, no modulo bias). Development adapter: SplitMix64 from seed 0, or FORTIS_DEV_SEED. *Effects: io, nondet.*
- `func seeded(self, seed: Int) Random`. A generator with its own deterministic sequence from seed (replay). *Effects: alloc, io.*

### `class Environment implements Authority`

- `func get(self, name: StringView) Secret[String]?`. The variable as a Secret, or null when unset or when name is empty or contains `=` (nondet). Development adapter: the process environment. *Effects: alloc, io, nondet.*

### `class Process implements Authority`

- `try func run(self, program: StringView, arguments: ListView[String]) Int`. Runs program with arguments to completion and returns its exit status (the `block` effect). Development adapter: starts no process; simulates `true` (0) and `false` (1) and refuses every other program with `process.denied`. *Effects: alloc, fail, block, io.*

### `class Supervisor implements Authority`

### `class Console implements Authority`

- `func print(self, text: StringView)`. Writes text and a line feed to standard output. *Effects: io.*

### `class RawSql implements Authority`

- `try func execute(self, statement: StringView) Int`. Runs one SQL statement and returns the affected row count. Development adapter: has no database; every statement fails `sql.unavailable`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1). *Effects: fail, block, io.*

### `class Capabilities`

### `class Host`

- `func capabilities() Capabilities`. The ten process-wide capabilities, created by one direct call in the entry main (11.6): every other use is rejected statically (E-EFF-010), and a second creation stops the run with the runtime-invariant defect (10.8) (E-EFF-010: LR 4.6). *Effects: none.*

### Functions and aspects

- `func reveal[T](secret: Secret[T], cap: SecretAccess) T`. The secret value (a copy); requires the SecretAccess capability (15); O(size). *Effects: alloc, io.*
